name: Pembrolizumab (anaplastic thyroid carcinoma, biomarker-selected)
cyclesNote: continuous every-3-week dosing until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or up to ~2 years; not a fixed cycle count

institution.provenance: ONCOTREE draft protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.io: favorable (high TMB, MSI-high / dMMR, or high PD-L1)
biomarkers.note: Checkpoint inhibitor used for BRAF wild-type anaplastic disease with a favorable immunotherapy biomarker, or added to continued BRAF/MEK blockade after BRAF-directed progression. Confirm the biomarker on validated testing.

supportiveCare: monitor for immune-related adverse events (pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathies including thyroiditis / hypophysitis, nephritis, skin) and manage per immunotherapy toxicity guidance.
check baseline and periodic thyroid, adrenal, and pituitary function.
may be combined with dabrafenib + trametinib after BRAF-directed progression, or given with cytotoxic chemoradiation.
continue multidisciplinary and palliative care with airway / symptom management.
monitoring: thyroid, adrenal, and pituitary function panels

doseModificationRules.text: Hold for grade 2 and most grade 3 immune-related events, start corticosteroids, and permanently discontinue for grade 4 or recurrent serious events per immunotherapy toxicity guidance. Obtain clinical review. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab
drugs.notes: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV over ~30 minutes on day 1 every 3 weeks (a 400 mg every-6-week schedule is an equivalent alternative), continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or about 2 years (per standard guidelines, general reference). Own wording - not a verbatim source copy.
